cornerCallouts: The cars are diving into the tricky Turn 1, a tight hairpin that demands precision and commitment.
Now they're navigating the esses of Turn 2 and Turn 3, where momentum is key to a fast lap time.
Next up is the sweeping Turn 4, a fast right-hander that tests the car's balance and the driver's nerve.
Into Turn 5, the bus stop chicane. A prime overtaking opportunity if you dare to brake late and be aggressive.
The exit of Turn 5 is crucial, setting up the run down the short chute to Turn 6.
Turn 6 is another hairpin, crucial to getting the run onto the oval section.
They're now powering through Turn 7, the final corner before entering the oval section and the finish line.
Watch the drivers carefully through the Turn 5 bus stop; it's a real car breaker if you get it wrong.
strategyPoints: Tire degradation will be a major factor on this 3.2km Roval. The abrasive surface and constant changes in direction will punish the rubber.
Fuel strategy will be critical. With a shorter lap than the oval, teams will be pushing to maximize their stints without compromising performance.
The pit window will be tight. A perfectly executed stop can gain valuable track position, but a mistake can be devastating.
Track position is paramount here. Overtaking can be difficult on the Roval, so starting up front is a huge advantage.
Look for teams to experiment with different tire compounds. The choice between softs and mediums could make or break their race.
With multiple braking zones, brake wear will be a concern. Teams will need to manage their brakes carefully to avoid fading later in the race.
The short lap length means traffic will always be a factor. Drivers will need to navigate the backmarkers strategically to avoid losing time.
Early safety cars could throw a wrench into everyone's strategy. Teams will need to be prepared to react quickly and decisively.
weatherCommentary: The Pocono Mountains can bring unpredictable weather. Keep an eye on those clouds, a sudden shower could change everything.
The humidity is high today, which will make the conditions even more challenging for the drivers and their equipment.
The wind is picking up, which could affect the car's handling, especially through the faster sections of the Roval.
The sun is beating down on the track, increasing the track temperature and affecting tire grip.
We're seeing a slight chance of rain later in the afternoon. That could make for a very interesting finish here at Pocono.
